Q: How to determine if a point is inside a triangle? A:

Let the inside of the triangle be the half space bounded its edges in counter-clockwise order. Then for any three points a, b, c, let the pair of directed line segments a->b and b->c be defined as a "left turn" if these lines considered as vectors (that is, b - a and c - b) have a positive cross product.

Point p is inside a triangle if and only if for all three of its edges s->t, the pair s->t and t->p are a left turn.
